mechanism.base: Wood tames earth, the old texts say, because the gathered thing wins over the scattered one: a single root goes down through loose soil and the whole hillside learns to stay put. The ground loses nothing by it. Held by roots it keeps its rain, its weight and its harvest, where bare soil would wash away in one hard season. What wood takes from earth it gives back as shape.
mechanism.catalyst_turn: With too little Earth, the roots have nothing to grip: all growth and no ground to claim, so the reach goes up and little stays yours. Pick one thing worth owning and get it.
mechanism.friction_turn: With too much Earth, the ground outweighs the roots: more to hold than one trunk carries, and it bends toward breaking while still saying yes. Rest before you take on more ground.

function.definition_catalyst: Your Action is what you go and build, claim and provide. Earth makes it steady, so what you claim lasts. As a catalyst, firm ground runs short and each gain counts for more than it should. You never quite feel you have enough put by.
function.definition_friction: Your Action is what you go and build, claim and provide. Earth gives it weight, so whatever you claim needs keeping. As a friction, what you take on grows heavier year by year. Holding it is how you feel secure, and over time you carry more than you finish.
function.definition_balanced: Your Action is what you go and build, claim and provide. Earth makes it steady, so what you claim lasts. In balance, firm ground holds under each new reach. Whatever you chase, something solid stays under your feet.
function.advise_catalyst: The ground under your plans is thinner than they need. Pick one goal for the season and give it the same hour each week. Ask one friend to check on your progress in a month.
function.advise_friction: Seek Wood, your own Body energy. Wood is the trunk under everything you reach for, the body that stands before it carries. Let it hold what Earth piles up. Your load has grown past what you can bear. Start each week by clearing out one thing you no longer use. Say no to one request before you say yes again.
function.advise_balanced: What you reach for and what you keep stay level while both get your hours. Mend one worn thing you own before you buy anything new. Pick one plan for the season and keep at it until the season turns.

candidates.cta_verdict: You build to keep rather than to show, and the things you go after slowly are usually the ones that stay yours.

catalyst.clause: The roots have nothing to grip: all growth and no ground to claim.
catalyst.remedy: Pick one thing worth owning and get it.

friction.clause: The ground outweighs the roots: more to hold than one trunk carries.
friction.remedy: Rest before you take on more ground.

wide.clause: Earth is all around you, the ground your roots were made for.
wide.remedy: Use it. Claim one plot and work it to the end.

missing.clause: No ground for the roots to take: growth that lands nowhere and claims nothing.
missing.remedy: Borrow ground: a budget, a lease, one thing paid off.

spared.clause: No Earth weighing on the roots, and the trunk stands straighter for it.
spared.remedy: Keep it that way: own little, carry less.

thin.clause: A little ground on the roots, light enough to hold without bending.
thin.remedy: Keep the load this size. Add nothing to it.

excess.clause: Earth piled past what roots can hold: the soil wins, and the trunk snaps under the weight.
excess.remedy: Set most of it down. Sleep, then lift one thing.

friction.clause: The holding never stops: every wall claimed, every trellis taken, roots spread past what the vine can feed.
friction.remedy: Hold less wall, hold it deeper.

mechanism_yin.base: The concentrated prevails over the scattered, and so wood governs earth: the root threads the loose soil, binds it, and holds the slope that rain would otherwise carry away. Ground without roots erodes grain by grain. Gripped by the living vine, the same ground becomes terrace, garden, land worth naming.
mechanism_yin.friction_turn: Run heavy, the holding never stops: every wall claimed, every trellis taken, roots spread past what the vine can feed. Hold less wall, hold it deeper.

__ore.retired_bonds_dip: You provide like ground provides: quietly, constantly, and without invoices.
__ore.retired_fn_body: The Drive is your action function: what you go get, build, and hold. With Earth running it, action in you is territorial and patient: you advance by rooting, compounding, refusing to be moved. What you claim you keep, and what you keep appreciates. Choose ground worth decades, because your way of holding makes leaving expensive.
__ore.retired_base_personal: Your core is Wood, and Wood tames Earth: roots hold the hillside. Earth is the solid, ownable ground your growth exists to take hold of: land, savings, positions, anything with acreage. That is why Earth is your Action, the arena of what you build and claim. A tree does not chase its territory. It roots into it and stays.

backlog_dips_tg_pattern.order: What you provide becomes order: the ground you tend sets where every path across it runs.

__ore.retired_v3_definition_catalyst:
Earth is your Action, and as a catalyst, it is where your reach becomes something held: savings, property, positions, commitments that stay put. You do best when ambition lands somewhere concrete.

Acquisitive in the healthiest sense: the paid-off tool, the account that only grows, the role kept long enough to compound. What you hold steadies you, and steadiness makes the next reach possible.

Ownership is ambition slowed down enough to keep. Automate a monthly amount into one long-term asset and stop renegotiating it. Review what you hold twice a year. Add slowly, and only what you intend to keep for a decade.
__ore.retired_v3_definition_friction:
Earth is your Action, and as a friction, it is holding past your means: too many commitments owned, maintained, and defended at once, each taxing energy you no longer have spare. Everything you keep charges rent on you.

Two storage units, four subscriptions, an acre of obligations, and a faint dread attached to each. The holdings that once felt like strength now read as weight, and letting go feels like losing even when it is relief.

Lightness is also a form of wealth. Sell, delegate, or close one standing obligation this month. Before acquiring anything, name its yearly cost in hours. Keep a short list of what you would defend in a hard year, and loosen everything off it.
